sections.title: How to play
sections.intro: Every arrow on the board points somewhere. Tap one and it slides away, but only if nothing stands in its way. Find the order that sets them all free, from a gentle first board to puzzles bigger than your screen.

items: Look where each arrow points. Its path runs straight on to the edge of the board.
Tap an arrow whose path is clear, and off it goes. Tap a blocked one and you lose one of your 3 hearts.
Clear every arrow to win. Clearing one can only ever free others, so no level turns impossible halfway.

items.title: Stuck?
items.text: A hint lights up an arrow that can leave right now. The first 3 are free, then they cost 30 coins.

items.title: A big board?
items.text: Drag to move around it, and pinch to see all of it.

items.title: 600 levels, 17 worlds
items.text: From Meadow to Starlight, each world with its own look, along one long map.

items.title: A hard level every 10th
items.text: Bigger, always a picture, played at night, and worth 30 coins.

items.title: New obstacles as you go
items.text: Rocks, bombs, ice, mirrors, portals, shutters and colour gates, each introduced as you reach it.

items.title: A daily challenge
items.text: One board a day, the same for every player, with rewards for each month.

items.title: Rooms with friends
items.text: Race 2 to 8 players on the same boards. Share a 6-character code and go.

items.title: Your own maps
items.text: Build levels, share them by code, and play the ones other players made.

sections.title: On your phone too
sections.intro: Exitwise is free on Android too. Sign in with Google in your browser and on your phone, and your progress, your name and your settings come with you.

items.a: Yes, in your browser and on Android. You earn coins by playing: 10 for a level, 30 for a hard one, and 5 more for a perfect clear.
No, you can play straight away. Signing in with Google keeps your progress and your settings on every device and puts your name on the leaderboards.
Yes. Every level comes from a fixed seed, so everyone gets the same board, and each one is tested to be solvable before it ships.
